column3: Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew does not explicitly add Your to the shield as BSB does.
The Hebrew has a command to shut or block, where BSB names a javelin.
The Hebrew explicitly names my soul; BSB says my life.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says he pursues them; BSB leaves the object unstated.
The Hebrew names a pit with their net in the first clause; BSB attaches the pit explicitly to digging in the second.
The Hebrew has him throughout; BSB uses them and adds they created to the final hazard.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly says stronger than he; BSB says aggressor.
The Hebrew says they question me; BSB describes making charges.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew has my prayer in the singular returning to my bosom; BSB has prayers returning unanswered.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew says they tore and were not silent; BSB describes slandering without ceasing.
The Hebrew explicitly names a cake in its mockery phrase; BSB says jesters at a feast.
The Hebrew names young lions and my only one; BSB has these lions and my precious life.
The Hebrew describes a mighty people; BSB says many people.
The Hebrew names an eye in the singular and does not explicitly add in malice to winking.
The Hebrew names words of deceit; BSB says deceitful schemes.
The Hebrew has mouth and eye in the singular and completed verbs; BSB has eyes and present verbs.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew calls for awakening with two verbs; BSB says awake and rise.
Close to the Hebrew.
The Hebrew explicitly names our soul and has their heart in the singular; BSB interprets the wish and uses hearts.
The Hebrew makes them the active subject putting on shame and reproach; BSB uses be clothed.
The Hebrew explicitly names His servant’s peace; BSB says well-being.
The Hebrew has praise in the singular; BSB has praises.
